subject: AI & Agents
title: Training vs Inference
description: A short lesson to help you apply Training vs Inference.

hook.text: Training is studying for the exam. Inference is taking it.

buildup.text: During training, a model adjusts millions of parameters to minimize errors.

discovery.text: Once trained, the model is frozen. Inference means applying what it learned to new inputs.

twist.text: Training GPT-4 cost over $100 million. Running a single query costs a fraction of a cent.

climax.text: You interact with AI at inference time — the expensive learning already happened.

punchline.text: Training is the homework. Inference is the exam.

quiz.question: What is inference in AI?
options: Applying a trained model to new data

details.summary: Training is when the model learns from data, adjusting millions of parameters over hours or months. Inference is when the trained model makes predictions — answering questions or classifying images in milliseconds.
details.whyItMatters: Training is expensive and slow; inference is cheap and fast. Understanding this distinction explains why developing AI costs billions but using it costs pennies per query.
takeaways: Training adjusts model parameters by processing training data
Inference uses the trained model to make predictions quickly
Training costs millions; inference costs fractions of a cent

faq.question: Why is training so much more expensive than inference?
faq.answer: Training processes the entire dataset multiple times, comparing predictions to correct answers and adjusting billions of parameters. Inference only does a single forward pass through the model for each prediction.

faq.question: Does a model keep learning during inference?
faq.answer: Standard models do not — they are frozen after training. Some advanced systems use techniques like in-context learning or retrieval augmentation to adapt at inference time without modifying model weights.
